root_cause.text: In the `DeleteIndexEntryRoot` case of `do_action` in `fs/ntfs3/fslog.c`, the entry size (`esize`) read from a log record is used without bounds checking, allowing an oversized value to compute an end pointer beyond the used buffer, causing `PtrOffset` to yield a negative offset that, when cast to `size_t` in `memmove`, results in a heap buffer overflow (slab-out-of-bounds read/write).
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a validation `if (PtrOffset(e1, Add2Ptr(hdr, used)) < esize) goto dirty_vol;` which ensures `esize` does not exceed the remaining used space, directly addressing the root cause described in both the CVE and commit messages.

vuln_statements.explanation: Entry size is read directly from the log record without any bounds checking, allowing an attacker-controlled oversized value to be used in subsequent pointer arithmetic.
Uses the unchecked esize to compute an end pointer, which can go beyond the allocated buffer and lead to an out-of-bounds condition.
Computes the length parameter via PtrOffset with an out-of-bounds e2 pointer, resulting in a negative offset cast to size_t (very large), causing a heap buffer overflow during the memmove.
